question: How much US online spending will Adobe report for Cyber Monday 2026?

calls.reasoning: Adobe's Sept 28 2026 forecast is $15.1B (+6.2% YoY on $14.25B). Over 2022-2025, Adobe's first-reported Cyber Monday figure came in at or slightly above its preseason forecast (+0.4% to +3%); in 2021 it came in 5% below. October tracking was on plan (Prime Day $9.86B vs $9.9B forecast, +8.5%). Median slightly above the forecast, ~15.2. Downside risks: Black Friday growing faster (+9.2%) and taking Cyber Monday share, cautious consumers. No Kalshi/Polymarket/Manifold market found.

- Adobe forecast vs actual, Cyber Monday: 2024 forecast $13.2B (+6.1%) vs actual $13.3B (+7.3%) (Spokesman/Adobe recap Dec 2024). From memory, not re-verified this run: 2025 forecast ~$14.2B vs $14.25B; 2023 ~$12.0B vs $12.4B; 2022 ~$11.2B vs $11.3B; 2021 ~$11.3B vs $10.7B (actual fell YoY).
- Prime Big Deal Days Oct 6-7 2026 actual $9.86B, +8.5% vs forecast $9.9B (Adobe via exclusivenewstoday).
- Adobe survey: 61% of shoppers spending more carefully over economic concerns; 40% trading down to cheaper brands (ppc.land, Sept 2026).
- Adobe revised the 2024 season base up $0.6B without explanation, so baselines can shift between reports.
- Status quo: Adobe publishes its Cyber Monday recap the next day (Dec 1); in recent years the first figure has come in near the preseason forecast.
- Resolves off Adobe's first published full-day Cyber Monday 2026 total (nominal USD, CM alone), rounded to $0.1B; not Cyber Week, not later revisions.
- Event window: Nov 30 2026 (single day); as of Nov 8 2026, 0% elapsed.
- Searched, absent: Kalshi/Polymarket/Manifold markets; Adobe November-to-date 2026 actuals.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same anchor ($15.1B Adobe forecast) and the same historical forecast-vs-actual pattern. Factual dispute: the 2023 preseason forecast (Runs 1/2 say $12.0B, Run 3 says $11.6B). I could not verify it with no web access; I lean toward $12.0B, and either way 2023 was an upside miss, so it only changes the error SD slightly. The 2021-2023 history is from the runs' memory and unverified, so I kept a ~3% error width. Medians of 15.15-15.25 are a judgment call; I take 15.2 (forecast x ~1.005-1.01 median historical ratio). I carry Runs 2/3's dispersion forward, trimmed slightly. No escape mass: leaving the range would take a 20%+ deviation, with no concrete mechanism.
